scope: Primary-source engineering supplement about operating examples and reproducible practices. This is not an overall greenest-facility ranking. Reported operation, counterfactual estimates, design ranges and expansion plans remain distinct. Undated pages carry an access date rather than an invented publication year. The October review retains its original cutoff.

sources.title: Thermosyphon Cooler Hybrid System for Water Savings in an Energy-Efficient HPC Data Center: Results from 24 Months and the Impact on Water Usage Effectiveness
sources.authors: David Sickinger; Otto Van Geet; Suzanne Belmont; Thomas Carter; David Martinez
sources.type: National laboratory technical report; field engineering evaluation
sources.methods: Twenty-four-month evaluation of thermosyphon hybrid cooling added to an operating warm-water HPC facility; comparison with estimated cooling-tower-only operation.
sources.finding: Hybrid dry and evaporative cooling reduced site water demand while preserving energy-efficient operation. Warm-water component cooling, chiller avoidance and heat reuse form the wider design.

metrics.boundary: Site cooling water versus continued heat-recovery and cooling-tower operation
metrics.status: Reported field result with counterfactual comparison

metrics.boundary: Same installation; includes the first-year saving and must not be added to it
NREL HPC data center
On-site cooling-water consumption / IT electricity
Estimated continuation of heat recovery and cooling towers
metrics.status: Counterfactual estimate, not a second observed facility

sources.limitations: Historical facility-specific results, not current fleet performance. Savings depend on weather, coolant temperatures, loading and comparison assumptions. Site WUE excludes electricity-supply water and does not establish lifecycle carbon or neighborhood health outcomes.
sources.access: Technical report and laboratory bibliographic record reviewed; DOI and five authors verified.

sources.title: Cooling unit saves half-million gallons of water at Sandia supercomputing center
sources.type: National laboratory news release reporting an engineering deployment
sources.methods: Laboratory account of the first six months of thermosyphon operation in 2019, attributed to the engineering project lead.
sources.finding: A second laboratory reports water and electricity savings after installing thermosyphon cooling. The device rejects heat when ambient conditions permit; conventional cooling remains necessary on hot summer days.

metrics.period: First six months of operation in 2019
metrics.boundary: Sandia supercomputing-center cooling retrofit
Cooling electricity; not the entire center's electricity use

sources.limitations: An official deployment account, not an independently reproduced whole-facility lifecycle assessment. Six-month savings should not be doubled into an annual estimate. The thermosyphon's operating season depends on local temperatures.
sources.access: Full official release reviewed; publication date and operating period verified.

sources.title: CSC Sustainability Report 2025

sources.methods: Annual facility energy, cooling-water and heat-recovery reporting, with PUE, WUE and ERE definitions.
sources.finding: LUMI combines warm-water cooling and useful heat recovery. Its reported 2025 heating output supplies about one-tenth of Kajaani's district-heating energy. Annual operating metrics differ from earlier promotional design values.

metrics.boundary: EuroHPC LUMI data center
Data-center cooling-water consumption / IT electricity; excludes upstream electricity water
LUMI heat-recovery accounting; not PUE
LUMI heat for Kajaani district heating

sources.limitations: Operator reporting, not identified here as externally assured. Heat reuse requires a nearby buyer and compatible network. Heat recovered does not erase original electricity use, upstream water, manufacturing emissions or backup-generator impacts.
sources.access: Annual report's facility table, definitions and heating explanation reviewed, PDF page 21.

sources.title: Google 2026 Environmental Report
sources.theme: electricity; carbon-free energy; energy efficiency; reporting
sources.geography: Hamina campus and Finland grid region; different boundaries
sources.methods: Campus annual PUE reporting and region-level hourly carbon-free-energy matching methodology.

metrics.boundary: Hamina, Finland campus
Google's Finland grid region, including grid and contracted CFE; not a campus lifecycle measure

sources.limitations: PUE does not measure computing usefulness or total consumption. Regional hourly CFE is neither a campus-specific emissions inventory nor zero lifecycle emissions. Keep report year, performance year, geography and assurance scope with each figure.
sources.access: Annual report PUE and regional CFE tables checked; metrics retain their separate boundaries.

sources.title: Power usage effectiveness
sources.methods: Quarterly and trailing-twelve-month campus and fleet PUE tables; accessed as a November 2026 snapshot.
sources.finding: Publishing repeated campus-level efficiency measurements allows a community to distinguish an operating record from a design target and check changes over time.
sources.limitations: Undated, changing webpage; access date is not publication date. Quarterly, trailing-twelve-month and annual figures must not be interchanged. PUE alone omits water stress, power-source emissions, hardware and community exposure.
sources.access: Live page's reporting structure and 2025 campus table reviewed; historical data may change.

sources.methods: Operator description of an operating campus, its infrastructure and heat-recovery project.
sources.finding: The campus reuses a former paper mill and seawater-cooling infrastructure and describes offsite heat recovery. Reusing infrastructure and locating near an appropriate cooling source are transferable design principles.

metrics.status: Operator expectation, not a verified annual delivered result

sources.title: Limitations to air free cooling in data centers under rising heat and humidity
sources.authors: Christina Karamperidou; Jake W. Casselman; Sean B. Cleveland; Damena Agonafer; Vivek V. Manepalli; Roshith Mittakolu; Lingnan Lin; Gerardo A. Rivera Tello
sources.methods: Historical hourly climate observations and climate-model simulations assess heat and humidity constraints on direct air-side economization.
sources.finding: Rising heat and humidity can reduce suitable hours for direct outdoor-air cooling. Future conditions need to inform siting and hybrid-system design.
sources.limitations: Climatic operability analysis, not a measured universal increase in facility electricity per degree. It does not cover every cooling architecture, humidity-control intervention or future adaptation.
sources.access: PubMed bibliographic record and abstract; publisher-indexed methods and scope reviewed.

sources.title: Tropical Data Centre (DC) Standard
sources.type: Government implementation guidance and operator case studies
sources.theme: tropical climate; cooling; efficiency; controlled operating trials
sources.methods: Guidance and case studies of staged temperature-setpoint changes with operating monitoring and customer coordination.
sources.finding: Singapore provides a tropical alternative to relocating all computing to cold climates: test safe temperature ranges and reduce unnecessary cooling while checking reliability.
sources.limitations: Case-study percentages concern different denominators such as total energy, cooling energy or fan energy. Do not generalize a fixed saving per degree, or infer low-carbon power or zero water. Full direct page access encountered JavaScript verification; indexed government case-study text and roadmap were reviewed.
sources.access: Government-indexed case-study text and official roadmap; full direct page access limited.

sources.theme: heat reuse; district heating; community infrastructure
sources.methods: Utility description of Qarnot liquid-cooled computing and its district-heating connection, with separate installed and future phases.
sources.finding: The first phase is described as operational, with 30 computing clusters and heat recovery up to 65 degrees Celsius for a district network.

metrics.boundary: Recovered heat at the network interface

sources.limitations: The roughly 800 thermal MWh/year first-phase figure is capability, not an audited annual meter result. The 16 GWh/year and 1,350-apartment figures concern future expansion. Displaced-fuel emissions require a counterfactual and heat-pump/pump accounting.

sources.title: The new social housing and office building of Gironde Habitat will be heated free of charge through Qarnot technology with BNP Paribas IT calculations
sources.venue: BNP Paribas press release; Gironde public housing plan
sources.theme: distributed computing; social housing; heat reuse; community benefit
sources.methods: Computing-customer account of installed radiator computers, corroborated by the later Gironde housing plan: https://www.gironde.fr/sites/default/files/2024-05/PDH_Gironde_ORIENTATIONS.pdf
sources.finding: 346 computing radiators link useful batch calculations with heat for a mixed office and social-housing building. Computing is placed where heat has a user.

metrics.period: Deployment described around building inauguration planned January 2019; later housing-plan corroboration
metrics.boundary: Gironde Habitat building
metrics.status: Deployment record, not annual energy measurement

sources.title: Life cycle analysis for emissions of scientific computing centres
sources.type: Peer-reviewed life-cycle simulation with real-centre inputs
sources.theme: lifecycle emissions; hardware lifetime; growth; heat reuse
sources.geography: Centre inputs from Sweden, Taiwan, Slovenia and United States
sources.methods: Twenty-year life-cycle scenarios compare growth, electricity mix, replacement and heat reuse. Public code/data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16894209
sources.finding: Replacement and lifetime decisions depend on manufacturing emissions and electricity carbon intensity. Expansion can dominate cumulative emissions despite improved efficiency.
sources.limitations: Scenario analysis, not an observed twenty-year intervention. Heat-reuse cases include hypothetical assumptions; displacement credits do not remove emitted CO2. Results require local workload, power and hardware inputs.
sources.access: Open publisher full text and reproducibility information reviewed.

sources.title: Design for circularity - a data centre equipment case study
sources.type: Peer-reviewed equipment analysis and comparative lifecycle model
sources.theme: circular hardware; repair; refurbishment; e-waste; lifecycle
sources.geography: European electricity/recycling assumptions; non-AI enterprise servers
sources.methods: Reverse-engineering and materials analysis combined with comparative LCA for a prototype circular server, reuse and refurbishment scenarios.
sources.finding: Modularity, replaceable components and reuse can lower modeled environmental burdens. A 16-year scenario reports about 29% lower overall weighted environmental impact.
sources.limitations: The 29% is a multi-category weighted result, not CO2-only savings. Operational energy is held equal. Prototype/model comparison, not sixteen observed years or proof for GPU hardware.
sources.access: Open publisher full text, publication date and outcome definition reviewed.
